extracted.intended_audience: authors and peer reviewers of medical case reports; medical journal editors
extracted.subtask_short: writing and reviewing medical case reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and peer-reviewing clinical case reports to ensure accurate, transparent, and useful reporting of individual patient cases for medical journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Support an increase in the accuracy, transparency, and usefulness of case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CARE guidelines exist to improve completeness and quality of case reports; use them as the foundation for author instructions and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagnosis or intervention of primary focus, with the words "case report".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the main diagnosis or intervention in the title and explicitly label the manuscript as a "case report" so readers and indexers can identify the report type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide between two and five topical keywords that describe the case to aid indexing and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an abstract that briefly states the background/context, summarizes the case, and presents the main conclusion or lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise introduction explaining the context and rationale for reporting the case (why it is noteworthy or educational).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient information
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identified patient demographics; primary concerns and symptoms; medical, family, and psychosocial history; relevant past interventions and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report identifying information in de-identified form and include the patient's chief complaints, relevant past medical/family/psychosocial history, and prior interventions with outcomes to allow understanding of the case context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant physical examination and clinical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe key physical exam findings and other clinical observations that informed diagnosis and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and current information from this episode of care, organized as a timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present chronological information (events, interventions, test results) from the episode of care in a clear timeline format to show sequence and timing; a table or figure can be helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic methods (physical examination, laboratory testing, imaging); diagnostic challenges; diagnostic reasoning including differential diagnosis; prognostic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which diagnostic methods were used, any challenges encountered, the clinician's diagnostic reasoning (including differential diagnoses considered), and prognostic features that affected decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Type (pharmacologic, surgical, preventive, self-care); administration (dosage, strength, duration); changes in intervention with rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the intervention(s) in detail including type, dosing/administration parameters, duration, and any subsequent changes with explanation of the reasons for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes; important follow-up diagnostic and other test results; intervention adherence and tolerability; adverse and unanticipated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both clinician-assessed and patient-reported outcomes, relevant follow-up test results, adherence/tolerability information, and any adverse or unexpected events, with timelines where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths and limitations; discussion of relevant medical literature; rationale for conclusions; main takeaway lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the case in relation to existing literature, acknowledge strengths and limitations of the report, provide the rationale supporting the conclusions, and clearly state the principal lessons or clinical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, the patient's perspective on their experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the patient's own perspective on their illness and care when available and appropriate to provide additional context and patient-centered insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that informed consent was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit statement in the manuscript that informed consent was obtained from the patient (or their proxy) for publication of the case details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic checking that all 13 items are present and adequately reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers should use the checklist to verify that each CARE item is present and sufficiently detailed; journals can incorporate the checklist into author guidelines and review workflows to ensure completeness and transparency.
